extracted.intended_audience: agents, brokers, web-brokers, Exchange administrators, and stakeholders responding to the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory amendments governing documentation of consumer consent, acceptable means to show review/consent, standards of conduct for marketing by agents/brokers/web-brokers on the Exchanges, prohibited marketing practices, monitoring/enforcement procedures, and related technical eligibility/verification updates for APTC/CSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer execution of HHS-approved consent form
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to §155.220(j)(2)(ii)(A) requiring documentation by agents, brokers, and web-brokers showing that eligibility application information has been reviewed and confirmed to be accurate by the consumer (or the consumer's authorized representative) must be effectuated by having the consumer or the consumer's authorized representative take an action to execute the HHS‑approved and created consumer consent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalizing execution of an HHS-created form aims to reduce interpretive variation, reduce consumer harm from noncompliant documentation, streamline review of noncompliant entities, and speed investigations and determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable and unacceptable actions to demonstrate review/consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(2)(ii)(A)(2) and §155.220(j)(2)(iii)(C) list acceptable actions: handwritten or electronic written signature or initials made directly on a document indicating consent, an email from the consumer or authorized representative, a recorded verbal conversation, or other clear and verifiable means; unacceptable actions include a signature simply typed on documentation or a filled-in checkbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handwritten signatures/initials are favored because they can be compared to other handwriting to verify authenticity; typed names or checked boxes do not clearly show the consumer personally reviewed and confirmed accuracy. The action must create a record that can be maintained and produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to document consumer consent prior to providing enrollment assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to §155.220(j)(2)(iii)(A) would require agents, brokers, or web-brokers to demonstrate that the consumer or their authorized representative has obtained and reviewed consent documentation by executing an HHS‑approved and created consumer consent form prior to providing enrollment assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This documentation must comply with regulatory requirements and produce a record that the agent, broker, or web-broker can maintain and produce to confirm consent was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required elements in consumer consent documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS has found consent documentation often lacks required information; documentation should include the name of the agent, broker, web-broker, or agency receiving consent; the name of the consumer or authorized representative; the dates of consent; the scope, duration, and purpose of the consent; and the process through which consent may be rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of these elements does not adequately demonstrate prior consumer consent and can lead to inaccurate eligibility determinations, missed plan correspondence, inability to access more suitable coverage, and unexpected tax liabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce eligibility application and consent documentation upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Current and proposed standards authorize HHS (or its designee) to periodically monitor and audit agents, brokers, and web-brokers and to request and review eligibility application information and consent documentation to determine compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents, brokers, and web-brokers must produce documentation upon request in response to monitoring, audit, or enforcement activities; failure to provide documentation has hampered investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketing standards of conduct: correctness and non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(ii) would require agents, brokers, and web-brokers to provide consumers with correct information about FFEs, QHPs offered through the FFE, and insurance affordability programs, not omitting material facts, and to refrain from marketing that is misleading, materially inaccurate, coercive, or discriminatory based on race, color, national origin, disability, age, or sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of the proposal, 'sex' is defined consistent with Executive Order 14168 as an individual's immutable biological classification as either male or female. These marketing standards align Exchange requirements with Medicare Advantage and aim to protect consumers and ensure uniform enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on cash or cash-equivalent inducements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(iii)(A) would prohibit agents, brokers, and web-brokers from providing cash, monetary rebates, gift cards, travel vouchers, or cash equivalents to induce consumers to enroll or for other purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a categorical prohibition on cash-equivalent incentives to induce enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on gifts: nominal value and broadly offered
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(iii)(B) would allow gifts only if they are of nominal value, offered to similarly-situated consumers without regard to enrollment, and are not in the form of cash or cash equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominal value is defined by the HHS Office of Inspector General and review would utilize the same prohibitions/allowances used in the Medicare Advantage Program; State laws on gifts remain applicable and termination for violations would be shared with States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false guarantees of zero-dollar premiums
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(iii)(C) would prohibit agents, brokers, and web-brokers from falsely asserting or suggesting that consumers will always qualify for zero-dollar insurance or zero-dollar premiums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such advertisements may mislead consumers to provide PII under false assumptions, risking unauthorized enrollments or misuse of PII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false or misleading use of government logos/notations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(iii)(D) would prohibit agents, brokers, and web-brokers from falsely using identical or facsimiles of government or other official logos and notations that could mislead consumers into believing material is government-approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends existing prohibitions (e.g., deceptive direct-enrollment websites) to advertisements and broader government identifiers beyond HealthCare.gov to prevent consumers from mistakenly providing PII to private entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on miscommunicating enrollment timelines and SEP deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(iii)(E) would prohibit agents, brokers, and web-brokers from miscommunicating enrollment timelines and deadlines, including providing false information related to Special Enrollment Period (SEP) deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inaccurate timelines may coerce premature enrollment and cause consumers to select plans they might not have otherwise chosen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on misconstruing legislation, regulations, or Executive Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(iii)(F) would prohibit agents, brokers, and web-brokers from misconstruing legislation, regulations, or Executive Orders, including listing fake/incorrect citations or using misleading characterizations of legal authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aims to reduce misinformation/disinformation in advertisements and ensure consumers are not misled before providing PII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false endorsements and AI-generated impersonations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(iii)(G) would prohibit the use of an image, likeness, or quote from a notable figure (including AI-generated deepfakes) in an advertisement claiming an endorsement when that endorsement is not truthful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes false attribution of quotes or fabricated endorsements; such behavior may also violate State or Federal laws on use of name/image/likeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for third-party-created marketing materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(v) would make an individual or entity described in §155.220(j)(1) responsible for ensuring that all marketing-related materials created, written, released, or produced by the individual or by entities or persons acting on their behalf adhere to §155.220(j)(3)(ii)-(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to agents or brokers working for another agent/broker, third-party marketing organizations contracted to create materials, and similar parties; supports HHS compliance actions against agents/brokers when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to produce marketing materials upon request (monitoring/audit/enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §155.220(j)(3)(iv) would require agents, brokers, and web-brokers to produce any marketing material upon request in response to monitoring, audit, and enforcement activities conducted consistent with related paragraphs of §155.220.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS does not propose a marketing-specific record-retention requirement because it expects to have access to marketing materials through monitoring/audit; production on request facilitates investigations and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial steps when misleading marketing is identified
rubrics_metrics.description: When HHS discovers misleading marketing, it may begin by engaging in technical assistance (TA) or move directly to enforcement; proposed remedial steps include requiring the agent/broker/web-broker to timely remove the misleading marketing and review CMS-provided materials on compliant marketing practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two remedial mechanisms (remove marketing; review CMS materials) are proposed to bring entities into compliance and educate them to prevent future incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a misleading-marketing scoring system to prioritize enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS currently uses an evaluation method with a scoring system based on the number of ads used in public marketing and the number of violations within each ad to determine whether to provide TA or pursue enforcement, with higher scores indicating more egregious noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This universal standard is intended to ensure equitable treatment across agents, brokers, and web-brokers and to prioritize cases involving a large volume of ads or multiple violations per ad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of a definitive connection between marketing and agent/broker for enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will seek a definitive connection between misleading marketing and an individual agent, broker, or web-broker before taking enforcement; connections can be made via contractual information, metadata containing contact information, or other reliable means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responsibility for posted marketing cannot be determined, enforcement is hindered; HHS plans to provide TA explaining its approach and to increase monitoring of social media and other sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and reconsideration procedures for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §155.220(g), HHS may terminate an agent's, broker's, or web-broker's Exchange agreement(s) for cause for sufficiently severe noncompliance or patterns of noncompliance; §155.220(g)(2)(i) references violations of any standard specified under the section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS provides 30 calendar days' notice and an opportunity to resolve findings; if not resolved, termination may follow; terminated parties can request reconsideration within 30 days and HHS must provide written reconsideration decisions within 60 calendar days of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed removal/sunset of the vendor training program (§155.222)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to remove §155.222, which currently governs the HHS-approved vendor program for delivering annual agent/broker training and information verification, effectively sunsetting the vendor program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: underutilization (only six entities have participated since inception), low share of training completions via vendors (~<10%), and estimated Federal savings of ~$300,000 per plan year; agents/brokers would still have access to training via CMS' Marketplace Learning Management System (MLMS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'eligible noncitizen' and APTC/CSR eligibility alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose adding a new definition of 'eligible noncitizen' at §155.20 (and cross-reference at 42 CFR 600.5) to mirror the 'eligible alien' definition in 26 U.S.C. 36B(e)(2)(B), and to amend eligibility rules so Exchanges grant APTC to U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, or eligible noncitizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These changes align Exchange eligibility and verification rules with section 71301 of the WFTC legislation; related CSR eligibility is affected because CSRs are only allowed for applicants eligible for PTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of eligible noncitizen status via SAVE and inconsistency process
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose adding verification regulations at §155.320(c)(3)(ix) requiring Exchanges to attempt to verify eligible noncitizen immigration status using Department of Homeland Security SAVE program data and to proceed with the inconsistency process in §155.315(f)(1)-(4) when SAVE cannot verify the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective for plan years starting on or after January 1, 2027; aligns Exchange verification with statutory changes and provides a clear verification pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical cross-reference updates for tax-filer family definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed technical update to §155.305(f)(1)(ii) to cross-reference 26 CFR 1.36B-1(d) so that a tax filer's potential APTC-eligible family members are defined consistent with Treasury regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns Exchange rules with Treasury regulations and clarifies who counts as a family member on whose behalf a tax filer may claim APTC, particularly given the elimination of personal exemptions on federal returns.
